subject: Retention vs Snapshot packaging — pricing simulation and staged discount ask
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@stratacorp.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Retention vs Snapshot packaging — pricing simulation and staged discount ask

Elena —

Thanks again for taking the time on the demo yesterday. As promised, I'm sending a concise packaging proposal and a simple cost model so your infra and finance teams can compare the two approaches we discussed: persistent retention (hot-path + archive) vs. snapshot-based retention (short live windows + periodic snapshots for analytics).

High-level ask / proposal:
- Pilot: 3-month canary on 3 dev projects (ingest ~15 GB/day) using the Snapshot package to validate query patterns.
- If snapshot pilot meets latency & query-replay needs, move to a tiered Snapshot SKU with an annual commit.
- If customer needs persistent KV caching + live trace retention, offer a Hybrid Retention SKU with a 12-month commit and a stepped discount schedule.

Attached: redwood-pricing-sim.xlsx (tabbed model: raw token estimates, storage delta, egress assumptions) and SOW-draft-retention-snapshot.pdf (pilot scope).

Questions for you (quick):
1) Do you prefer a single blended SLA across both approaches or separate SLAs for Snapshot vs Retention?
2) Any hard constraints on data residency or encryption beyond standard KMS?
3) Who on your side would own the pilot acceptance criteria?

Next step: Ben (cc'd) will share an example concession ladder we typically use for pilots converting to annual commitments. If this looks good to you, we can pencil in an internal handoff and a pilot kickoff the week of May 18.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pricing-sim.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: SOW-draft-retention-snapshot.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@stratacorp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@stratacorp.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Retention vs Snapshot packaging — pricing simulation and staged discount ask

Monica —

Appreciate the clear summary and the model. Quick answers while I run this by our infra lead (in ops@):

- SLA: we prefer separate SLAs. The analytics team will accept a longer tail for snapshot rehydration but latency for live debugging must be < 250ms p95.
- Residency: must stay in US regions only. KMS with customer-managed keys required.
- Pilot acceptance: ops@stratacorp.com will own the acceptance criteria; I will align them with product.

A couple of follow-ups from finance:
- The snapshot approach appears cheaper at baseline, but they asked for a worked example where we see 20%+ growth in ingested span volume month-over-month — can you scenario that?
- What concessions are typical for a mid-year commit vs a full-year commit?

If you can post a sensitivity table in the spreadsheet for 15/20/30% ingestion growth, that would help us. We'll also need a simple example invoice line showing retention vs snapshot monthly charge so our procurement can see monthly cadence.

On timing: pilot week of May 18 is fine but we need the sensitivity table before we lock in.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Sr. Observability Lead, StrataCorp

Elena / Monica —

Thanks for the fast feedback, Elena. Attached is a quick concession ladder we typically offer for scenarios like this (I added a sample invoice line at the bottom of the sheet). Highlights: 

- Pilot-to-annual conversion: we can provide a transition credit equal to 50% of pilot fees applied to the first 3 months of the annual commit when you commit within 30 days of pilot completion.
- Growth protection: for teams forecasting >=20% monthly ingest growth, we suggest a 3-tier overage bracket that caps effective unit price increases beyond committed volume (gives you predictability while we provision capacity).
- Snapshot vs Retention baseline: snapshot is about ~35% cheaper on storage for low-query rehydrate customers; hybrid retention narrows that gap once KV caching reduces token cost by 10–18% in active debugging workloads.

Per Elena's ask, Monica — I added sensitivity rows for 15/20/30% monthly growth and an illustrative invoice line for May (pilot month) vs June (first committed month). If you want, I can drop a short note that procurement can sign to accept the concession ladder as an appendix to the SOW.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
